messages:
mira: Repro from a user on Deno + Cloudflare: ESM import of our SDK throws at runtime "fetch is not defined" despite global fetch being present. Strange.

oliver: Probably a bundler or type mismatch. Do we ship any DOM ambient types?

jin: We don't currently publish a minimal fetch ambient .d.ts. Consumers without lib.dom enabled will get TS errors for RequestInit/Response.

mira: Proposed quick fix: runtime resolver that prefers globalThis.fetch, falls back to dynamic import('undici') in Node, and emits a friendly error if neither is present.

jin: For types, ship `types/fetch-ambient.d.ts` with a tiny `declare global { function fetch(input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>; }` then include it in the package types. Safe and non-intrusive.

oliver: Also add package.exports mapping for esm/cjs to help require/import consumers. And CI smoke tests: node cjs, node esm, deno run, and a worker runtest.

docbot: Note created: RDW-7722 (sdk: fetch fallback + ambient types).

nora: I'll update onboarding sample apps to show 1) Node polyfill snippet and 2) edge/no-polyfill example. That should reduce initial support tickets.

mira: one last edge: Next.js Edge can inline-strip dynamic imports. Add a synchronous check that throws an explanatory error linking docs rather than obscure stack.

jin: I'll open two small PRs: fetch-resolver + tests, and types-only. We can cut a patch after CI.

mira: thanks all :rocket:
